verdict.rationale: ImageMagick ships its own security-policy mechanism (selectable Open, Limited, Secure and Websafe policies via policy.xml) that can disable script-like coders such as MVG and MSL and the URL delegates. Community evidence shows that without such configuration these inputs are interpreted: the ImageTragick RCE came from a URL delegate passing user input into a shell call, and SVG/MVG are processed by logic resembling a small command interpreter. Safe handling of untrusted input therefore depends on operators hardening the policy, not on inert-by-default behavior. missing for 10: documented guarantee that scripts/macros are treated as content by default, first-party docs detailing which coders the Secure/Websafe policies block, independent corroboration that the hardened policies prevent execution.

support.subject: As an ops lead, the converter treats untrusted input safely: scripts and macros are read as content, never executed

citations.quote: you can choose and customize one of these security policies: Open, Limited, Secure, and Websafe.
